title: Database Credentials Standard
definition: Software programs may access internal databases only after authentication with credentials.

title: Database Credentials Standard
definition: Authentication credentials must not reside in clear text or easily reversible encryption in the main executing body of a program's source code.

title: Database Credentials Standard
definition: Database credentials must not be stored in a location accessible through a web server.

title: Database Credentials Standard
definition: Algorithms must meet the standards in NIST FIPS 140-2 or any superseding document applicable on the implementation date.

title: Database Credentials Standard
definition: Use of RSA and Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC) is strongly recommended for asymmetric encryption.

title: Database Credentials Standard
definition: Database usernames and passwords may be stored in a file separate from the executing body of the program's code, but that file must not be world-readable or world-writable.

title: Database Credentials Standard
definition: Database credentials may reside on the database server; in that case, a hash function number identifying the credentials may be stored in the executing body of the program's code.

title: Database Credentials Standard
definition: Database credentials may be stored as part of an authentication server, such as an LDAP entitlement directory, and database authentication may occur on behalf of a program during user authentication.

title: Database Credentials Standard
definition: Database credentials must not reside in a web server's documents tree.

title: Database Credentials Standard
definition: Passwords or passphrases used to access a database must adhere to the Password Policy.

title: Database Credentials Standard
definition: When database usernames and passwords are stored in a non-source-code file, they must be read from that file immediately before use.

title: Database Credentials Standard
definition: Immediately after database authentication, memory containing the username and password must be released or cleared.

title: Database Credentials Standard
definition: The scope used to store database credentials must be physically separated from other code areas, such as by placing the credentials in a separate source file.

title: Database Credentials Standard
definition: A credential file must contain only the credentials and any functions, routines, or methods used to access them.

title: Database Credentials Standard
definition: For languages executed from source code, the credentials source file must not reside in the same browsable or executable directory tree as the executing body of code.

title: Database Credentials Standard
definition: Each program, or collection of programs implementing a single business function, must have unique database credentials.

title: Database Credentials Standard
definition: Credentials must not be shared between programs.

title: Database Credentials Standard
definition: Database passwords used by programs must be treated as system-level passwords as defined by the Password Policy.

title: Database Credentials Standard
definition: Developer groups must maintain a process ensuring that database passwords are controlled and changed in accordance with the Password Policy.

title: Database Credentials Standard
definition: The database password management process must restrict knowledge of database passwords to a need-to-know basis.

title: Database Credentials Standard
definition: Users and software accessing sensitive data must be subject to proper access control and should not be able to perform privileged operations outside their authorized scope.
